# Book I, Proposition 39

*Equal triangles on the same base*

> Equal triangles which are on the same base and on the same side are also in the same parallels.

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/I/39-idea.svg" alt="If two triangles on the same base (red) are equal in area (yellow), the line through their tips runs parallel to the base (blue)." width="420"></p>

<p align="center"><em>If two triangles on the same base (red) are equal in area (yellow), the line through their tips runs parallel to the base (blue).</em></p>

## Euclid's proof

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/I/39.svg" alt="Euclid's figure for Proposition I.39, with Heath's letters" width="360"></p>

Let ABC, DBC be equal triangles which are on the same base BC and on the same side of it;

[I say that they are also in the same parallels.]

And [For] let AD be joined;

I say that AD is parallel to BC.

For, if not, let AE be drawn through the point A parallel to the straight line BC, [I. 31] and let EC be joined.

Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle EBC; for it is on the same base BC with it and in the same parallels. [I. 37]

But ABC is equal to DBC; therefore DBC is also equal to EBC, [C.N. 1] the greater to the less: which is impossible.

Therefore AE is not parallel to BC.

Similarly we can prove that neither is any other straight line except AD; therefore AD is parallel to BC.

Therefore etc.

## In Lean

✅ Proved

From [`Elements/BookI/Prop39.lean`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop39.lean). Euclid's sentences are the `--` comments; the lines under each one are the Lean that carries it out.

```lean
/-- Equal triangles which are on the same base and on the same side are also in the same parallels. -/
theorem Prop39 {A B C D : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDBC : Triangle D B C)
    (heq : △ A B C = △ D B C) (hside : SameSideOf A D B C) (hAD : A ≠ D) :
    AreParallel A D B C := by
  -- Let ABC, DBC be equal triangles which are on the same base BC and on the same side of it;
  obtain ⟨BC, hB, hC⟩ := Postulate1 B C hABC.ne₂₃
  -- [I say that they are also in the same parallels.]
  -- And [For] let AD be joined;
  /- The parallel drawn through A will pass through D, and so be AD. -/
  -- I say that AD is parallel to BC.
  -- For, if not, let AE be drawn through the point A parallel to the straight line BC, [I. 31]
  /- The parallel through A is the straight line K (`Prop31.line`), which Euclid
     calls AE once E has been found. -/
  obtain ⟨K, hA_K, hKBC⟩ := Prop31.line (hABC.bca.off_line hB hC)
  -- and let EC be joined.
  /- E is where the parallel meets BD; that they meet at all is I.30
     (`Prop30.meet`). -/
  obtain ⟨BD, hB_BD, hD_BD⟩ := Postulate1 B D hDBC.ne₁₂.symm
  have hD_BC : ¬ OnLine D BC := hDBC.bca.off_line hB hC
  have hBD_BC : BD ≠ BC := fun e => hD_BC (e ▸ hD_BD)
  obtain ⟨E, hE_BD, hE_K⟩ := Prop30.meet hKBC hB hB_BD hBD_BC
  have hE_BC : ¬ OnLine E BC := hKBC.not_onLine hE_K
  have hEBC : Triangle E B C := (Triangle.of_line hB hC hABC.ne₂₃ hE_BC).cab
  obtain ⟨EC, hE_EC, hC_EC⟩ := Postulate1 E C hEBC.ne₁₃
  -- Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle EBC; for it is on the same base BC
  -- with it and in the same parallels. [I. 37]
  have h37 : △ A B C = △ E B C :=
    Prop37 hABC hEBC ⟨K, BC, hKBC, hA_K, hE_K, hB, hC⟩
  -- But ABC is equal to DBC; therefore DBC is also equal to EBC, [C.N. 1] the greater to the
  -- less: which is impossible.
  have h1 : △ D B C = △ E B C := CommonNotion1 heq.symm h37.symm
  /- The parallel puts E on A's side of BC, hence on D's side. Since E is on
     BD, it lies on the ray from B through D. -/
  have hEB : E ≠ B := fun e => hE_BC (e ▸ hB)
  have hED_side : SameSideOf E D B C :=
    (SameSideOf.of_line hABC.ne₂₃ hB hC (hKBC.sameSide hE_K hA_K)).trans hside
  have hray : OnRay E B D :=
    OnRay.of_sameSideOf hED_side ⟨BD, hB_BD, hD_BD, hE_BD⟩ hEB
  /- Euclid's figure has E between B and D, so that EBC is the less; Proclus'
     other case has E beyond D, so that DBC is the less. Either way only D
     itself will do (`OnRay.eq_of_area_eq`). -/
  have hED : E = D := hray.eq_of_area_eq hDBC h1.symm
  -- Therefore AE is not parallel to BC.
  /- A parallel meeting BD away from D has been excluded: the parallel
     through A must pass through D itself. -/
  have hD_K : OnLine D K := hED ▸ hE_K
  -- Similarly we can prove that neither is any other straight line except AD; therefore AD is
  -- parallel to BC.
  have hpar : AreParallel A D B C := AreParallel.of_parallel hAD hABC.ne₂₃ hA_K hD_K hB hC hKBC
  -- Therefore etc.
  exact hpar
```

## Mishnah

**A partial converse.** Heath: "This theorem is of course the *partial* converse of I. 37." I.37's base and its conclusion, equal areas, are the hypotheses here, and its parallels the conclusion. One hypothesis is new: "The additional qualification in this proposition that the triangles must be *on the same side* of the base is necessary because it is not, as in I. 37, involved in the other hypotheses" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 337). Equal triangles on opposite sides of BC need not make AD parallel to BC, so our statement has a `SameSideOf` hypothesis; it asks too that A and D be two points, for Euclid joins AD.

**"I say that they are also in the same parallels."** Heath's note on this bracketed sentence reports Heiberg's proof, from a papyrus fragment, that it was added by someone who took "And let AD be joined" for part of the construction, and so thought the thing to be proved should be stated first; the same hand altered "And" into "For". Our `--` lines keep both brackets as Heath prints them.

**Where E falls.** Through A, I.31 draws the parallel to BC, and Euclid's E is where it meets BD. That it meets BD at all comes from I.30 (`Prop30.meet`): BD meets BC at B, so it meets the parallel to BC, as in I.37. I.37 then makes ABC equal to EBC. So the certificate cites I.30 besides Euclid's I.31 and I.37, with Common Notions 1 and 5; Postulate 5 comes in through I.29, by way of I.30 and I.37.

**"The greater to the less."** Common Notion 1 makes DBC equal to EBC, and to call one the greater Lean must know where E is. The parallel puts E on A's side of BC, and so on D's: on the ray from B through D (`OnRay.of_sameSideOf`). If E is between B and D, as in Heath's figure, `area_lt_of_cut` makes EBC less than DBC, by Common Notion 5; if E is beyond D, a case Proclus finds equally easy (Heath, vol. 1, p. 337), it makes DBC the less. So BE equals BD, E is D, and the parallel through A is AD; Book Zero's `OnRay.eq_of_area_eq` makes this argument once, for I.40 too. Our figure draws AE level, as the proof supposes; Heath draws AD level.

**The modern way.** Put B at (0, 0) and C at (c, 0), with c positive: a triangle on BC with vertex (x, y) has area ½c|y|. Equal areas give equal |y|, and the same side of BC gives y the same sign, so A and D are at one height and AD is parallel to BC.
